meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here. 4:15, and I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. You asked for this meeting, Hale. Why was my son's mark changed before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Procedure 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark consequence is entered, and nobody called me. So you've told me what went wrong. What are you proposing to do about it?
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me, Hale. Turn the screen toward me and tell me what it is, who made it, and what date is on it. I'm writing down whatever you say.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 with 612 words, and 11:58 with 794. Whose account is this history from, and is there anything in it before that night? Owen told me he wrote this over the weekend, so I want to see for myself what the history shows.
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
"Anywhere in the history." That's one document, Hale, and a history only shows what happened inside it. Did you ask Owen where he did his drafting before you entered the zero, yes or no?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

October 15, an outline arguing cowardice, and an essay that says "epistemological paralysis." I'm writing that down, and I want both documents in front of me, not described to me. A student can change his argument between an outline and an essay, Hale, and you still haven't answered my question: did you ask Owen about any of this before you entered the zero?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

I'm writing down "Act 3, Scene 2" and the line, and I will search the play myself tonight. A student can misremember a quotation, Hale, and a wrong line is not a finding. For the third time, did anyone ask Owen about it before the zero went in?
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Okay. You also still haven't answered me, and I've asked three times. What are you proposing, Hale, and will you put those documents in my hands before I leave?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.

September 24, in-class writing, next to the essay. Give it to me and let me read it myself, because I'm not taking your word on what it shows. And tell me what you say the difference is, Hale, in your own words, so I can check it against the page.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.
I know what 4.4 says, Hale. I printed it. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, and I want that in writing before anything else is discussed.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.

Lunch in your room, with the door closed, is the first sensible thing you've said. Before I agree to anything: the zero comes off the gradebook today, since he can see it on his phone, and the rewrite covers the same outcomes as the essay, as 4.4 says. Put "nothing goes on file" in an email to me and the principal, Hale, and then we'll talk about a date.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

You're asking me to write your email for you? Fine. The zero comes off today, the rewrite replaces it, and "nothing goes on file" reaches me in writing, copied to the principal, by end of day tomorrow. I also want copies of the edit history, the October 15 outline, and the September 24 writing, and then I'll agree to the rewrite to put this behind him.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Tonight, then. I'll be watching for it, Hale, and the principal will be copied. Anything else you need to say, or have we finished?
Is there anything else you want me to include?
You have my terms, Hale. The zero off, the rewrite replacing it, "nothing goes on file" in writing, and the copies. Put the date and time of the rewrite in the email too, and don't make me ask twice.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Eight tonight. I'm writing that down, Hale. If it isn't in my inbox, I'm in the principal's office tomorrow morning.
Thank you for coming in.
Don't thank me yet. Thank me when the email arrives. Is there anything else, Hale?
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.

Is that the rewrite, or a conversation? If it's the rewrite, the zero is off the gradebook before he sits down, and that goes in your email with the time. If it's a conversation, Hale, he hears from you that it's being fixed, not from his phone.
